summary.intent: Manage the v1.1 milestone's hardening block (phases 51-55) from a single terminal: discuss all 5 phases, plan them in parallel isolated git worktrees, then ship Phase 51 through the full verify/secure/validate/simplify/CodeRabbit/ship loop before touching other phases.
summary.outcome: All 5 hardening phases discussed and planned in parallel worktrees (21 total plans, all plan-checker green). Phase 51 executed, shipped as PR #529 after catching a desktop build break (unwrap_key cascade) plus 5 CodeRabbit zeroization findings, and diagnosing+fixing a critical S3 zeroization regression that broke all multi-publish IPNS operations in E2E CI.

repo: GSD executor's commit style ('feat 51-03:', 'test 51-01:') is non-conventional and trips the repo's pr-release-preview CI check on any commit touching versioned packages — requires git filter-branch reword before merge; will recur on phases 52-55
pr-release-preview scans individual commit subjects (not just PR title), so lint-pr-title passing does not mean Release Preview passes
required_signatures is false on main, so filter-branch rewrites don't require re-signing 30+ commits

cargo test -p cipherbox-fuse does not compile cross-crate consumers (cipherbox-desktop, cipherbox-sdk), so type-signature changes can break the desktop crate silently even when all in-phase tests pass
winfsp feature cannot compile on macOS (winfsp-sys build script + windows_core errors) — Windows-only FUSE changes must be validated through CI

Background GSD agents CAN nest sub-agents on Claude Code — general-purpose/claude agents have Tools: * including the Agent tool; the manager workflow's 'no nesting in background' guardrail is stale for this harness
GSD commit helper reports commit_failed as a false negative while the commit actually lands — always verify with git log --oneline -1, never retry

GSD #683 auto-degrade: execute-phase runs sequentially in the current worktree when shouldDegrade is true (HEAD diverged from origin/HEAD), bypassing per-plan worktree isolation — this is actually desirable when the worktree already has deps installed
core.hooksPath is an absolute path to the main tree's .husky directory, so all worktrees share the same hooks and need their own node_modules (pnpm i in each worktree, not a symlink)
pr-release-preview bot may push a chore(release) commit after the check passes — fetch+rebase required before any subsequent force-push to the branch

code.finding: S3 plan incorrectly added params.ipnsPrivateKey.fill(0) in the finally block of createAndPublishIpnsRecord. This function is called by publishWithCas (which reuses the same buffer on retries) and by folder ops (which cache the key in folderTree for the session lifetime). Zeroing a caller-owned buffer caused all 2nd+ publishes to derive pubkey from zeros → wrong IPNS name → 400. The fix is to NOT zero here; every caller (shared-write, vault, bin) zeroes its own transient key. This restores the pre-Phase-51 contract documented in cas.ts: 'publishWithCas NEVER zeroes... callers are responsible'.

Guard tests were written that asserted createAndPublishIpnsRecord zeroes the key — they encoded the bug as a test expectation and needed inversion to assert caller-ownership (key NOT zeroed by callee).

The 400 errors in E2E ('publicKey does not correspond to the given ipnsName') came from this pre-existing check, not from S1's new CID/sequence validation. The S1 diagnostics all showed passing — this was a red herring during root-cause investigation.

S3's unwrap_key return type change to Zeroizing<Vec<u8>> cascaded to this desktop consumer that the executor's cargo test -p cipherbox-fuse gate never compiled. Originally fixed with .to_vec() (hotfix), later properly fixed to store Zeroizing directly when the SDK state field type was changed (CodeRabbit #3).
root_folder_key field changed to RwLock<Option<zeroize::Zeroizing<Vec<u8>>>> (CodeRabbit #3). Cascaded to mount_filesystem params in both fuse/mod.rs:79 and fuse/windows/mod.rs:41.

Two separate CodeRabbit findings fixed: (#6) folder-key cache type changed to HashMap<String, Zeroizing<Vec<u8>>> — the old code had a misleading 'cleared when dropped' comment but stored raw Vec; (#7) spawn_file_meta_reencrypt source_key_arr/dest_key_arr changed from [u8;32] to Zeroizing<[u8;32]>.
Three identical base64 decode-and-map-err blocks in verify_ipns_resolve_signature deduplicated into a local closure (simplify finding applied; 6/6 api-client tests confirmed green).
publishWithCas passes the same params.ipnsPrivateKey buffer on every retry — makes createAndPublishIpnsRecord a invalid place to zero the key.
Generates a fresh transient keypair here; zeroes keypair.privateKey itself at lines 331-333. Confirmed that removing zeroization from createAndPublishIpnsRecord does not leak this key.

workflow: Mocking parseIpnsRecord in unit tests bypasses the real marshal→unmarshal round-trip — the CID round-trip was suspected as the E2E failure cause but was actually clean; the mock gave false confidence that S1 was correct when the real regression was in S3

Parallel vitest E2E suites can make failures look timing-dependent when they are actually deterministic — ipns-consistency failed 7/7 both in parallel and in isolation, confirming a logic bug not a race

Worktree isolation for parallel GSD planning: git worktree add <path> <branch>, then pnpm i inside — each worktree gets independent deps, husky hooks run normally, no git index collisions between concurrent planning agents
When a background agent is cut off by a session limit, check git log to see how far it got before resuming — both cut-off agents had committed their work before being interrupted

CodeRabbit CLI local review (coderabbit review --agent --base main --type committed) returned 0 findings after fixes were applied, confirming resolution before ship; the PR-level review is separate and may differ

git filter-branch --msg-filter with a sed pattern targeting 'type NN: ' subjects is the practical non-interactive bulk reword approach (interactive rebase is not available); drops commit signatures but acceptable when required_signatures is false

friction: Two session-limit interruptions mid-work — both times background agents had committed before cutoff, but required manual verification of git state before resuming

Worktree setup for parallel agents was iterative: first tried symlink for node_modules (wrong), then discovered pnpm i was correct; husky absolute hook path was a non-obvious consideration
